# Pendulum: repairing a date/time library without a test suite

I have been leaning on this library all over an application, and after picking up a recent checkout a great deal of everyday behaviour has gone wrong. The repository has received 20 separate undocumented edits. Nothing about the calendar changed and nothing in my own code changed: the same calls that used to give right answers now give wrong ones, and in several places a call that used to hand back a value now raises instead. Everything below is what I could pin down from the outside, set out by what I was doing when it went wrong.

Getting hold of a value from something outside my own program is the first thing that breaks. Anchoring a moment to a bare numeric offset rather than a named region — 6, 0, 5, -5, 9.5 — fails outright with a lookup error, and so does anything that needs one indirectly: reading text carrying an explicit offset, adapting an offset-bearing value handed over by another library, restoring a pickled value built that way, and comparing two such offsets for equality. Named regions such as `America/Toronto` or `Europe/Paris` are unaffected. Where one can be built at all, a negative offset reports a malformed name, minus five or minus five and a half no longer coming out in the `-05:30` / `-05:00` style, while positive offsets still look right.
